messages:
Emily: Quick question — for the new internal routing API for model serving, are we going proto-first (gRPC + protobufs) or keeping JSON/REST at the edge? Constraints: browser clients, per-customer quotas, console telemetry (token-level), and very smooth rollouts/rollback UX.
Jon: Proto-first internally sounds best to me. Stronger contract, smaller payloads, easier to add streaming. But we need an edge translation layer for browser & third-party integrators.
Priya: Agreed on proto-first for services, but quotas/rate-limits should be enforced at the gateway level (we can't trust all services to implement consistent per-tenant quotas). Envoy + external auth or a sidecar quota service would do.
Luca: Two worries: 1) telemetry fidelity — console needs per-route and per-token latency/costs. 2) rollout ergonomics — how do we canary model variants + routing policy without exploding config?
Emily: For telemetry, could we have the gateway attach trace/telemetry headers and emit a unified event stream? Eg, gateway adds x-rd-request-id and x-rd-token-cost which downstream services copy back.
Priya: Example header propagation idea:
```
# gateway -> service headers
x-rd-request-id: <uuid>
x-rd-tenant: <tenant-id>
x-rd-quota-key: <key>
# service copies x-rd-token-cost: 123 to response for gateway to aggregate
```
Jon: If we go proto-first, we also get typed routing metadata (via protobuf Any/metadata) which helps decisioning in the router. But browser clients need grpc-web or a REST gateway that transcodes. That transcode layer is where quotas + auth live.
Luca: Can we standardize a small set of routing metadata fields so gateways + console can reason about routes without decoding entire proto? e.g., model_id, route_version, cost_estimate.
Emily: Yes — define a "routing header bag" in proto and require adapters to map to HTTP headers for gateway use. That keeps the runtime fast and the console simple.
Priya: About rollouts: propose a routing policy config that supports weight-based rollouts and header-based overrides. Keep policy small and declarative so Console can edit it. Example: `route_policy = {match: tenant, weight: {v1: 80, v2: 20}}`.
Jon: Implementation patterns: 1) Sidecar-per-service doing proto natively + central gateway for external clients. 2) Central gateway does all auth/quotas/transcode and talks HTTP/1.1 JSON to services (least friction for browsers). 3) Hybrid: gateway transcodes to gRPC for internal mesh and falls back to JSON when needed.
Luca: Hybrid seems pragmatic. We avoid double-implementation on services. Gateway can call gRPC for mesh-native services and fallback to REST JSON for legacy ones.
Emily: Telemetry and tracing — we must ensure gateways attach an immutable routing fingerprint. Console can join traces and display per-route SLOs and token usage.
Priya: For quotas, we should avoid per-request synchronous quota checks on the critical path for latency-sensitive calls. Use local token buckets + async reconciler for accuracy. Gateway can enforce strict limits for obvious abuse.
Jon: For schema evolution: keep backward compatible proto rules and add a stable gateway API for transcode. Use method-level feature flags for canary.
Luca: UX notes for Console: expose a rollout slider that updates route_policy weights in the control plane and pushes to gateway; show real-time traffic split and error rates. Also a one-click rollback.
Emily: Edge case — webhooks and third-party integrations that expect plain JSON. We'll need auto-transcoding and a consistent error model (HTTP status + structured error body).
Priya: Ops question — where do we store routing policies? Central control plane (DB + versioned commits) with per-gateway caches; consistent rollouts via STAGED->CANARY->GA states.
Jon: We should author an RFC: proto routing bag, gateway header mapping, quota enforcement model, telemetry envelope, and rollout controlplane. Then do a small spike: gateway transcode + envoy filters + sample console slider.
Luca: I'll volunteer to spike the envoy filter that maps routing metadata to headers and emits a routing fingerprint metric.
deploy-bot: canary-config applied to staging gateways (build #2026.4.11). Observability hooks enabled. :rocket:
Emily: Awesome — Luca + Jon + Priya, let's sync tomorrow 10am to agree on required proto fields and basic gateway contract. I'll draft the RFC tonight and ping the channel. :thumbsup:
